speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. To determine the cause, how many days old are you, and has this vomiting occurred after every feed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia.

The patient's presentation of bilious vomiting within six hours of birth, combined with the specific finding of a younger sibling having pyloric stenosis, raises a critical differential for intestinal obstruction. While the sibling's history suggests a genetic predisposition to obstruction, the immediate onset of symptoms in a newborn with bilious emesis is the hallmark of a proximal intestinal blockage. I have already asked if the vomiting occurred after every feed; the current clinical picture strongly points toward a structural anomaly of the duodenum. To confirm this, I will request an abdominal X-ray to look for the classic "double bubble" sign.
